description: The image displays two pie charts illustrating the breakdown of error types in a dataset, likely from a study on generalization from atomic skills to complex reasoning tasks, as suggested by the paper title. The charts are accompanied by a legend at the top that defines four categories: “Atomic Skill Fail” (dark teal), “Correct” (medium teal), “Reason Error” (light teal), and “Question Misunderstood” (white). The left pie chart is divided into four segments: “Atomic Skill Fail” at 68.0% (dark teal), “Correct” at 12.0% (medium teal), “Reason Error” at 12.0% (light teal), and “Question Misunderstood” at 8.0% (white). The right pie chart also has four segments, but the “Correct” category is visually obscured by a gray rectangle, and its percentage is not readable; the visible segments are “Reason Error” at 21.0% (light teal), “Question Misunderstood” at 14.0% (white), and “Atomic Skill Fail” at 10.0% (dark teal). Both charts include percentage labels directly within their respective slices. The left chart’s segments appear to be ordered in descending size, while the right chart’s segments are arranged in a clockwise order from the largest visible slice (Reason Error) to the smallest (Atomic Skill Fail).
